A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sustained viral response reduces liver-related mortality and liver-related morbidity among patients with chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis, but alcohol overuse remains a risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma and decompensation after sustained viral response.

the treatment of HCV with DAAs is associated with a reduction in the incidence rate of liver-related complications, but that alcohol consumption is associated with an increased risk for HCC in the treated patients, even after achieving sustained virological response.

The main takeaway from our work is that

patients with chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis who achieve a sustained virologic treatment response have a reduced risk of liver-related morbidity (decompensation, hepatocellular carcinoma) and mortality.
patients with chronic hepatitis who have achieved SVR have a reduced risk of developing liver-related morbidity compared with patients who do not have SVR.

patients with CHC cirrhosis who have achieved sustained virologic responses have a reduced risk of liver-related morbidity, including hepatocellular carcinoma and liver decompensation, compared to patients who have not achieved sustained virological response.
